language_wrapper:
For each integer n in the range [{n_start}, {n_end}], let A(n) be the set of ordered pairs (i, j) with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n and i divides j, and let T(n) be the set of ordered triples (i, j, k) with 1 ≤ i < j < k ≤ n and i divides j and j divides k. Consider real variables x_1, x_2, ..., x_n in [0, 1] constrained by the equality Σ_{i=1}^n x_i = floor(n/3) + {delta}. Define

d(n) = max over x_i ∈ [0,1], Σ x_i = floor(n/3) + {delta} of [ Σ_{i=1}^n x_i^{p} − {lambda} · Σ_{(i,j)∈A(n)} (x_i x_j)^{q} − {mu} · Σ_{(i,j,k)∈T(n)} (x_i x_j x_k)^{q} ].

Compute the exact value of S = Σ_{n={n_start}}^{n_end} d(n).
teacher_generator_code:
def generator(rng):
    # Choose a nontrivial range for n
    n_start = rng.randint(60, 220)
    span = rng.randint(150, 300)
    n_end = n_start + span
    # Choose exponents ensuring convexity of Σ x_i^p and superlinear interactions
    p = rng.choice([3, 4, 5])
    q = rng.choice([2, 3])
    # Penalty coefficients (not trivial)
    lam_choices = [0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, rng.randint(2,5)/rng.randint(6,13)]
    mu_choices = [0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, rng.randint(2,7)/rng.randint(8,15)]
    lam = rng.choice(lam_choices)
    mu = rng.choice(mu_choices)
    # Fractional addition to floor(n/3): keep small to guarantee feasibility and non-integer sum
    # Ensure delta in (0.05, 0.49) for difficulty and fractional leftover
    delta = round(rng.uniform(0.08, 0.48), 3)
    # Sanity check: ensure feasibility holds for the entire range (s(n) <= ceil(n/2))
    # s(n) = floor(n/3) + delta
    for n in [n_start, (n_start + n_end)//2, n_end]:
        s = (n // 3) + delta
        cap = (n + 1) // 2  # ceil(n/2)
        if s > cap + 1e-12:
            # Rare, but retry if constraint fails
            return generator(rng)
    return {
        'n_start': n_start,
        'n_end': n_end,
        'p': p,
        'q': q,
        'lambda': lam,
        'mu': mu,
        'delta': delta
    }
hardness_rationale: We introduce a global mass constraint Σ x_i = floor(n/3) + δ, higher exponents (p ≥ 3, q ≥ 2), and triple-chain penalties over i|j|k. This turns the seed’s edge-only maximization into a constrained convex optimization problem on a divisibility hypergraph. Solving it requires recognizing that the divisibility poset’s upper half is an antichain of size ceil(n/2), then invoking convexity (or majorization/Karamata) to show that, under the sum constraint and 0–1 bounds, the optimal no-penalty configuration is k ones and one fractional remainder, yielding k + r^p per n. The need to combine poset structure (antichain selection avoiding all pair/triple penalties) with constrained convex maximization is a significant elevation in difficulty compared to the seed.
notes: Proof of correctness: For each n, let M(n) = ceil(n/2) be the size of the antichain H(n) = {i ∈ [1..n] : i > n/2}. Any i ∈ H(n) has no proper multiple ≤ n, hence no pairs (i, j) with i|j exist within H(n); similarly, no chains i|j|k lie entirely within H(n). By assumption Σ x_i = s(n) := floor(n/3) + δ ≤ M(n), we can place all mass on distinct indices in H(n), ensuring all pairwise and triple penalties vanish (the interaction sums are zero). Consequently, d(n) equals the maximum of Σ x_i^p subject to 0 ≤ x_i ≤ 1 and Σ x_i = s(n). Since t ↦ t^p is convex and increasing for p > 1, the sum of pth powers under a fixed sum is maximized by concentrating mass: set k = floor(s(n)) variables to 1, one variable to r = s(n) − k, and the rest to 0. A two-variable variant shows a^p + b^p ≤ (a + b − 1)_+^p + 1 when a + b ≥ 1; an inductive application of such transfers (moving mass from fractional entries into fewer entries up to the 1 ceiling) yields the claimed extremal form. Therefore d(n) = k + r^p and S = Σ_{n=n_start}^{n_end} [ floor(n/3) + δ − floor(n/3) ]^p + floor(n/3) simplifies to Σ ( floor(n/3) + (δ)^p when the fractional part is δ at each n, except when floor shifts; generally compute per n: k + r^p with k = floor(s), r = s − k. Since the constructed solution achieves zero penalties and the interaction terms are nonnegative multipliers subtracted from the objective, any configuration incurring penalties cannot surpass this value, completing the proof.
source_question: Given positive integer \(n \geq 3\), \(x_1, x_2, \cdots, x_n \in[0,1]\), consider the set \(A=\left\{(i, j)\left|1 \leq i<j \leq n, i, j \in \mathbb{N}^*, i\right| j\right\}\), let \(d(n)\) be the maximum value of \(x_1^4+x_2^4+\cdots+x_n^4-\sum_{(i, j) \in A} x_i^3 x_j^3\). Find \(\sum_{k=3}^{2025} d(k)\).
